structured.target: Val Amiel Vestil Kwentong Kalikasan Association of Young Environmental Journalists
structured.school_or_org: Association of Young Environmental Journalists (AYEJ); Val Amiel Vestil is a Silliman University College of Mass Communication alumnus and AYEJ founder/executive director
structured.program_event: Philippine Resilience Awards (PRA) 2025 — youth champion category; supported by the Climate Change Commission and partners (Senator Loren Legarda initiative, 2023+)
structured.theme_or_track: Kababaihan at Kabataan: Katuwang sa Paghahabi ng Isang Matatag na Bayan (PRA 2025 theme)
structured.what_it_does: Kwentong Kalikasan is a 14-episode video-advocacy project (documentary anthology plus TV-magazine series) that uses hope-based visual storytelling to put a human face on forest conservation in Northern Mindanao. Documentaries profile conservationists, indigenous youth, rangers, and green entrepreneurs in Bukidnon and Misamis Oriental; TV-magazine episodes use games and intimate conversations on biodiversity, sustainability, and climate resilience. Distributed via AYEJ social channels, partners (e.g. Probe Media Foundation, Knowledge Channel), and school film festivals.
structured.place: Philippines — AYEJ based in Cagayan de Oro City; series content focused on Bukidnon and Misamis Oriental (Northern Mindanao)
structured.outcome_or_award: Named a 2025 Philippine Resilience Awards youth champion for Kwentong Kalikasan (one of five youth champions recognized during Global Warming and Climate Change Consciousness Week). AYEJ as an organization has also been publicly associated with a WWF Philippines Force of Nature Award (org-level, not specifically verified as tied only to this series).
structured.gap: No public source found linking this project specifically to Ateneo Youth CLAP as a program name or cohort. Full production credits (directors, crew, all co-creators) beyond Vestil/AYEJ and Forest Foundation Philippines not fully listed in the articles used. Exact PRA ranking beyond “youth champion among five” not published. AYEJ website (ayej.org) was suspended when checked, so org-page primary text could not be re-verified. Force of Nature (WWF) details and year not fully documented beyond social posts.
structured.note: Strong CCC/PRA fit for Youth CLAP desk research even without an explicit “Youth CLAP” label: Vestil was honored under CCC-supported PRA 2025 for climate-resilience storytelling. Mechanism is communications/advocacy (not a hardware climate-tech product). Useful student-team angles: hope-based climate framing (problem→solution, victim→hero), DepEd/Knowledge Channel distribution, NCCT child-friendly assessment, partnering with a foundation grantee model, Mindanao forest + indigenous narrative focus. Vestil also publicly framed as AYEJ founder/ED and has prior recognition (e.g. ASEAN Youth Eco-Champion via Silliman alum coverage).
